items.title: BPCL approves ₹1.27 trillion refinery-petrochemical complex in Andhra
items.rss_summary: State-owned Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) has approved an investment of Rs 1,26,656 crore, with an estimated cost variation of 20 per cent, to set up an integrated greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Ramayapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, marking a major expansion of its refining and petrochemical footprint. The project, to be implemented through a wholly owned subsidiary, will comprise a 9 million tonnes per annum (MMTPA) refinery and a 1.5 MMTPA mixed-feed ethylene cracker, along with downstream petrochemical units, according to a stock exchange filing. The integrated complex will have a total processing throughput of 10.5 MMTPA and a petrochemical intensity of about 34 per cent. The project cost is more than 26 per cent higher than the initial estimate. The board approved the project at its meeting on Saturday. items.title: Delhi HC bars Old Monk makers from bottling 'iQ' gin in similar packaging
items.rss_summary: The Delhi High Court has restrained Old Monk makers from bottling its 'iQ' gin in a get-up which is deceptively similar to that of 'Greater Than' gin. The high court clarified that Mohan Meakin Limited, which manufactures Old Monk and iQ gin, is not restrained from using the mark 'IQ' or its 'iQ' device for gin or for any other goods and added that the company was at liberty to sell its gin in a different get-up. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav said plaintiff Nao Spirits And Beverages Private Limited, which manufactures and sells 'Greater Than' gin, has no monopoly over the colours black and white, and the defendant (Mohan Meakin) is free to use them in a manner which does not result in a get-up deceptively similar to that of the plaintiff. Equities, the rupee and government bonds have all rallied, signalling a shift in market sentiment from risk-off to risk-on. However, sustaining the gains into 2027 will require stronger domestic growth expectations and an improvement in banking-system liquidity, which could remain constrained as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) tightens monetary policy amid elevated inflation, the global brokerage said. items.title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri again after Bengal sample fails
items.rss_summary: Food regulator FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a packaged drinking water sample collected from its West Bengal plant failed laboratory testing, sources said. The sample tested positive for coliform bacteria, they added. This form of bacteria can enter water systems through sewage leaks or damaged pipes, among other pathways. This action marks the second instance of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) sanctioning prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd, a leading player in the packaged drinking water sector in the country. On Sunday, the FSSAI announced similar legal proceedings after a sample from one of Bisleri's plants in Goa also failed testing. The West Bengal sample was taken from a plant in Jalpaiguri's Telipara village. The presence of coliform bacteria was confirmed by both primary and referral laboratories. items.hinglish_title: Bengal plant ka sample fail hone par FSSAI ne Bisleri ke khilaf phir manzoor kiya prosecution
items.explanation: Food regulator FSSAI ne West Bengal plant ka packaged drinking water sample fail hone par Bisleri International ke khilaf legal action ki manzoori di hai. Jalpaiguri ke Telipara plant se liye gaye iss sample mein coliform bacteria paya gaya hai, jo primary aur referral labs dono mein confirm hua. FSSAI ne batch number PB 201 ki sale par rok laga di hai. Isse pehle Goa plant ke sample fail hone par bhi FSSAI ne aisi hi karyavahi ki thi.

Central bank ne iske liye ek uniform aur time-bound procedure tay kiya hai jisse aise accounts ki pehchan jaldi ho sake. Is naye niyam ka maqsad aam aur genuine customers ko kisi pareshani se bachana bhi hai.

items.title: Adani Group eyes airline investments months after ruling out airline entry
items.rss_summary: The diversified Adani group, which runs multiple airports across the country, has requested the government to allow it to invest in the airline sector, a top official said on Friday. Group chief finance officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh told reporters that over 60 crore people in the country can fly, and the number of daily flights needs to go up by nearly 10 times to 30,000. "And that's why we requested the government to at least allow us to invest, so that we can facilitate the development of airlines. Some fund, some other airline company and things like that...or an entrepreneur who wants to go into that space," the CFO said while speaking on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit here. In July this year, the group said it was "not evaluating any proposal to enter the airlines business". items.hinglish_title: Adani Group Ab Airlines Sector Mein Investment Ki Bana Raha Yojna
items.explanation: Desh bhar mein kai airports chala rahe Adani Group ne airline sector mein investment karne ke liye sarkar se ijaazat mangi hai. Group CFO Jugeshinder Robbie Singh ne bataya ki desh mein 60 crore log fly kar sakte hain aur daily flights ko lagbhag 10 guna badhana hoga. Isse pehle group ne airlines business mein direct entry se inkar kiya tha, par ab wo fund ya doosri companies ke zariye invest karne ka rasta talash rahe hain.

items.title: WazirX on Bitcoin's Recovery and its Liquidity Test

It's trading near USD 61,654 with Ethereum at around USD 1,729. Both remain sensitive to shifting risk appetite and the strength of spot demand.

Filhal Bitcoin kareeb USD 61,654 par aur Ethereum lagbhag USD 1,729 par trade kar raha hai. Dono hi assets market ke risk appetite aur spot demand par kafi depend kar rahe hain.

Karmachariyon ke hak ko surakshit rakhne ke liye yeh ek ahem ruling maani ja rahi hai.

items.title: BPCL commissions integrated lube blending plant, base oil terminal in Maha
items.rss_summary: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) has commissioned an integrated lube oil blending plant and base oil terminal at Rasayani in Maharashtra, strengthening its manufacturing and supply-chain infrastructure as the state-run energy major seeks to expand its MAK Lubricants business. The facilities, inaugurated on November 21 by BPCL chairman and managing director Sanjay Khanna, bring together base oil receipt and storage, lubricant blending, product filling, warehousing and dispatch within a single integrated operational complex, according to a company statement. The new infrastructure is expected to improve manufacturing flexibility, inventory management and supply reliability, while allowing BPCL to respond more efficiently to changing customer requirements and market demand. items.hinglish_title: BPCL Ne Maharashtra Me Shuru Kiya Naya Lube Blending Plant Aur Base Oil Terminal

items.title: Sebi aims to cut FPI onboarding time to five business days: Chairman
items.rss_summary: Markets regulator Sebi is aiming to reduce the onboarding time for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) from several months to as little as five business days through digital workflows and system integration, its chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Friday. Addressing the 17th Capital Markets Conference organised by ASSOCHAM, Pandey said the regulator has also proposed removing the additional disclosure framework for FPIs, bringing India's regulatory framework closer to global standards. "Through digital workflows and system integration, we aim to cut FPI onboarding from months to as little as five business days," Pandey said. Over the past few months, Sebi has taken several measures to ease the compliance burden for FPIs. Under the SWAGAT-FI (Single Window Automatic and Generalised Access for Trusted Foreign Investors) initiative, around 740 FPIs, accounting for nearly 17 per cent of FPI assets under custody, have registered. "SWAGAT-FI gives trusted, low-risk FPIs single-window .

items.title: Britannia Industries CMO Puneet Das quits within 10 months of joining
items.rss_summary: Leading bakery foods company Britannia Industries on Friday said its Chief Marketing Officer, Puneet Das, has resigned to pursue an opportunity outside the organisation, according to a regulatory filing. Das, who joined Britannia in February 2026, will be relieved from the company's services with effect from the close of business on December 9, 2026, according to a regulatory filing. "Puneet Das, Chief Marketing Officer, has decided to pursue an opportunity outside Britannia and has resigned from the services of the Company," said Britannia. Das was appointed Chief Marketing Officer of Britannia Industries effective February 16, 2026. His exit comes less than 10 months after taking charge of the marketing function at the biscuit and bakery major.

items.title: Nestle India receives ₹36.36 lakh EPFO demand, including ₹20 lakh penalty
items.rss_summary: FMCG major Nestle India on Friday said it has received a demand of Rs 36.36 lakh from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), including damages and a penalty of over Rs 20 lakh for the period 2012-2019. The order has been issued by the Regional Office of EPFO, Mysuru, under section 7Q and 14B of the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, the company said in a regulatory filing. "The company has received an order from the Regional Office of Employees' Provident Fund Organisation demanding an amount of Rs 36,36,548, which includes an amount of Rs 20,09,516 on account of damages/penalty for the period of 2012-2019 under PF Code," it said. The order, received by the company on November 26, 2026, has no material impact on its financials, operations or other activities, the filing added.
